title: Exponential growth: the last doubling
bigIdea: Constant proportional change turns tiny beginnings into enormous outcomes; doubling times, logarithms, and resource limits reveal when that story applies.

concepts.title: The last doubling fills the bottle
concepts.summary: A bacterium doubles every 20 minutes in an idealized bottle that is full at noon. The bottle was only half full at 11:40.
concepts.intuition: Run the film backward and a full bottle becomes half a bottle in just one generation.
misconceptions: Half full means half the total elapsed time has passed.
An almost empty bottle guarantees plenty of time remains.
visualHooks: A tiny smiling bacterium beside a huge bottle
A clock jumping from 11:40 to noon

concepts.title: Multiplication instead of addition
concepts.summary: Exponential growth multiplies by the same factor over equal time intervals. From 1 cell, five doublings produce 32 cells.
concepts.intuition: Each generation copies the entire crowd, so the amount added grows along with the crowd.
misconceptions: Doubling adds two individuals each step.
A rising straight line and an exponential curve describe the same rule.
visualHooks: Rows of 1, 2, 4, 8 colored cells
A staircase whose risers double in height

concepts.title: Doubling time is a clock
concepts.summary: For N(t)=N0 exp(kt), the doubling time is ln(2)/k. A constant doubling time means a constant proportional growth rate.
concepts.intuition: A doubling time counts how long it takes the entire graph to climb to twice its current height.
misconceptions: Doubling time becomes shorter just because there are more cells.
The rate 0.1 per day means an exact ten-day doubling for continuous growth.
visualHooks: Equal horizontal gaps between heights 10, 20, 40
A ruler marked in generations rather than cells

concepts.title: Interest earns interest
concepts.summary: Compounding applies each new percentage to principal plus accumulated interest. At 10% annually, 100 becomes 121 after two years.
concepts.intuition: Interest is a new worker that starts earning interest of its own next year.
misconceptions: Ten percent for two years always gives exactly twenty percent total growth.
An annual nominal rate determines the outcome without a compounding convention.
visualHooks: Coins sprouting smaller coin trees
Bars labeled 100, 110, and 121

concepts.title: Continuous growth and e
concepts.summary: Continuous proportional growth satisfies dN/dt=kN and has solution N0 exp(kt). Its rate k is not the same as the effective per-period fractional increase.
concepts.intuition: Zoom into a growth curve until each tiny rise is proportional to the height already there.
misconceptions: A continuous rate k=1 means only 100% total growth in one time unit.
Discrete and continuous rates with the same numeric value always agree.
visualHooks: A tangent arrow that lengthens with the curve height
Compounding intervals shrinking toward a smooth curve

concepts.title: A log scale turns ratios into distances
concepts.summary: On a logarithmic vertical axis, equal distances represent equal ratios. A positive exponential becomes a straight line whose slope encodes its growth rate.
concepts.intuition: A log axis folds each doubling into the same visual step, however enormous the population becomes.
misconceptions: A straight line on a log plot means the population adds a constant number.
Zero and negative values fit on an ordinary real logarithmic axis.
visualHooks: A ladder labeled 1, 10, 100, 1000
A curved growth trace straightening on log paper

concepts.title: Epidemics as branching generations
concepts.summary: In a simple generation model, each infected person produces R further infections on average. Early growth can be approximated by I(g)=I0 R^g when conditions remain stable.
concepts.intuition: Follow one branch of transmission and then imagine the same branching rule repeated at every tip.
misconceptions: R0 is a fixed property of a pathogen independent of population and context.
R0=2 means cases double every day regardless of generation interval.
visualHooks: A transmission tree with two branches per node
Generation clocks beneath branching clusters

concepts.title: Resources bend the curve
concepts.summary: The logistic model dN/dt=kN(1-N/K) slows growth near carrying capacity K. It approximates resource feedback rather than allowing exponential growth forever.
concepts.intuition: The crowd still makes new members, but every new member also takes away a little of the room left to grow.
misconceptions: A carrying capacity forces an abrupt universal stop at a fixed time.
Logistic growth adds the same number at every population size.
visualHooks: A bottle filling while food icons disappear
An S-curve approaching a dashed capacity line

concepts.title: Decay uses the same machinery
concepts.summary: Exponential decay removes a constant fraction in equal time intervals. For N=N0 exp(-λt), half-life is ln(2)/λ.
concepts.intuition: Rewind a doubling story and each equal tick removes half of whatever remains, not half of the original pile.
misconceptions: A half-life means all material is gone after two half-lives.
Every individual atom decays at exactly the half-life time.
visualHooks: A pile shrinking from 80 to 40 to 20
Independent glowing atoms switching off at random times

concepts.title: Know when the model stops working
concepts.summary: Exponential models are useful over intervals where proportional rates remain roughly stable. Changes in resources, behavior, or mechanisms can change the rate and invalidate extrapolation.
concepts.intuition: A formula is a local story about a mechanism, and its ending changes when the mechanism changes.
misconceptions: An excellent fit to early data guarantees indefinite exponential growth.
A slowing observed curve uniquely proves logistic resource saturation.
visualHooks: A forecast cone widening beyond observed dots
A growth engine with a changing rate dial
